title: Newton's first law: why you lurch forward when a bus brakes
examples: Why do I fall forward when the bus stops?

forces.label: Brakes
forces.ask: Why do I lurch forward when the bus brakes?

explain.say: Imagine you are standing on a bus in São Paulo, and the driver suddenly brakes. Whoosh, you lurch forward! But nothing pushed you forward. So what happened? A rule called Newton's first law explains it.

draw.text: Newton's first law: why you lurch forward when a bus brakes

forces.label: Brakes
forces.ask: Why do I lurch forward when the bus brakes?

explain.say: Look at you on the board, riding along with the bus. The down arrow is your weight. The up arrow is the floor pushing back. They are equal, so we call them balanced. Balanced forces do not change your motion. Are the two arrows the same size?

Yes, they match! Now see the arrow on the bus, pointing backwards. That is the brakes, slowing the bus. Your feet only grip a little, so your body carries on forward at the old speed. You did not speed up: the bus slowed down under you.

forces.label: Brakes
forces.ask: Why do I lurch forward when the bus brakes?

explain.say: That is Newton's first law: things keep still, or keep moving at the same speed in a straight line, unless an unbalanced force acts. This stubbornness is called inertia. A ball on smooth ice glides a long way. Why does a ball on grass stop sooner?

Because grass gives more friction, well done! That is why seatbelts matter: they give your body the backward force it needs when a car stops. Wow fact: the Voyager 1 probe has coasted through space since 1977, because almost nothing out there slows it down.

forces.ask: Why do I lurch forward when the bus brakes?

faq.q: Why do I lurch forward when the bus brakes?
faq.a: The brakes slow the bus, but no force slows your body at first, so it keeps moving forward at the old speed. That is inertia.
asks: Why do I fall forward when a car stops suddenly?

faq.a: An object stays still, or keeps moving at the same speed in a straight line, unless an unbalanced force acts on it.
Inertia is the way objects resist changes to their motion. The more mass something has, the more inertia it has.
Balanced forces are equal in size and opposite in direction. They cancel out, so the motion does not change.
asks: What happens when forces are balanced?

faq.q: How do seatbelts use Newton's first law?
faq.a: In a crash the car stops but your body keeps going. The seatbelt supplies the backward force that slows you down safely with the car.

facts: Newton published his three laws of motion in 1687 in the Principia.
Voyager 1 was launched in 1977 and is now in interstellar space.

options.say: Keeps going at the same speed

quiz.why: With no unbalanced force, an object keeps moving at the same speed in a straight line.

wrong.0: Slowing needs a force like friction, which is missing here.
wrong.1: Speeding up needs a forward force.

quiz.say: Which word means an object's resistance to changes in its motion?
quiz.show: Which word means an object's resistance to changes in its motion?
quiz.why: Inertia is the tendency of an object to keep doing what it is already doing.

wrong.1: Friction is a force that opposes sliding.
wrong.2: Gravity is the pull between masses.
